modules.title: Variables & Data Types
modules.description: Learn how to create variables and work with different data types in Python.

checkpoints.title: Predict variable values
checkpoints.summary: Trace variable assignments and predict the output.
checkpoints.description:
Look at the code below and predict what will be printed. Think about how variables store and change values.

Focus on the order of assignments.
checkpoints.starterCode:
# Python
x = 5
y = x
x = 10
print(y)
print(x)

checkpoints.title: Fix the type error
checkpoints.summary: Debug code with a type mismatch.
checkpoints.description: The code below tries to combine a string and a number but causes an error. Fix it so it prints the message correctly.
checkpoints.starterCode:
# Python
age = 25
message = "I am " + age + " years old"
print(message)

testCases.hint: Use str() to convert the number to a string

checkpoints.title: Swap two variables
checkpoints.summary: Write code to swap values of two variables.
checkpoints.description:
Given two variables `a = 10` and `b = 20`, swap their values so that `a` becomes 20 and `b` becomes 10. Then print both values.

Try to do it without using a third variable!
checkpoints.starterCode:
# Python
a = 10
b = 20
# TODO: Swap the values

print(a)
print(b)

testCases.hint: Python allows tuple unpacking: a, b = b, a

checkpoints.title: Reflection
checkpoints.summary: Reflect on what you learned about variables.
checkpoints.description:
Write a short reflection (2-4 sentences) about:
- What surprised you about how variables work?
- What's the difference between a variable's name and its value?

Check if year 2024 is a leap year and print "leap" or "not leap".

modules.title: Functions & Parameters
modules.description: Learn to write reusable code with functions, parameters, and return values.

message = greet("Alice")

checkpoints.summary: Debug a function that doesn't return correctly.
checkpoints.description: This function should return the square of a number, but it prints instead of returning. Fix it.

    print(n * n)

result = square(5)
print(result)

testCases.hint: Replace print() with return

checkpoints.title: Default parameters
checkpoints.summary: Write a function with default parameter values.
checkpoints.description:
Write a function `power(base, exp=2)` that raises base to the power of exp. If exp isn't provided, it should default to 2 (squaring).

Print `power(3)` and `power(2, 3)`.
checkpoints.starterCode:

# TODO: Write power function with default exp=2

print(power(3))
print(power(2, 3))

testCases.hint: Use def power(base, exp=2): and base ** exp
